name: Glowforge Aura
tagline: Consumer-friendly CO₂ laser with the simplest setup: at a subscription cost
tldr: Glowforge's compact CO₂ laser designed for crafters. Easy software, quick setup, and decent cutting for thin materials. The catch: premium hardware price plus required subscription for full features, and a smaller work area than xTool P2.

priceRange.note: Plus mandatory Premium subscription (~$50/mo) for full functionality

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: Strong on acrylic and wood versus diodes on the same budget tier
Integrated cabinet helps contain the beam and everyday smoke versus open-frame diodes
Software listed on the profile: test your workflow (LightBurn or maker app) on scrap first
cons: Ventilation to the outside is mandatory for regular cutting, not an optional upgrade
Tube life and replacement cost are part of the true ownership budget
beginnerNotes: This profile covers Glowforge Aura. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks before buying, then compare nearby models on the Compare page.
proTips: Factor subscription cost over 2–3 years into your budget. Proofgrade materials are convenient but expensive: third-party plywood works with testing. Aura is craft-scale, not sign-shop scale.
primaryUse: Simple CO₂ cutting and engraving for crafters who prioritize ease of use over power and cost efficiency.
mainObjective: Easiest CO₂ setup for crafters who want zero tinkering

editorialDepth.advantages: Glowforge Aura is built for acrylic signage, thick wood, and shop production once exhaust is sorted. 6.8W adds headroom on panels and multi-pass jobs.
editorialDepth.limitations: Avoid without ducting, for occasional gifts only, or if budget ignores tube replacement, power, and floor space. Bare metal without an IR accessory stays out of scope.
